cases.answer: The Thai Hypertension Society consensus estimates apparent treatment-resistant hypertension (apparent treatment-RH) at about 5.3% of the treated Thai hypertensive population. This derives from a nationwide 2014–2015 survey of 65,667 hypertensive patients in 833 hospitals, in which 17.1% were on ≥3 BP-lowering medications and 31% of those were not at BP target (systolic <140 and diastolic <90 mmHg). The estimated true RH in the Thai hypertensive population is around 3.4% of the treated population. The underlying assumption is that pseudo-RH accounts for 33–37% of apparent treatment-RH — as reported in other populations — and that the same proportion holds in the Thai population ('Suppose the same is true in the Thai population'). The authors note this 3.4% estimate is lower than the roughly 5% estimate from a meta-analysis of observational studies in other populations, which they also cite as a reasonable general estimate of true RH.

claims.claim: The consensus estimates apparent treatment-RH at 5.3% of the treated Thai hypertensive population, based on a 2014–2015 nationwide survey (65,667 patients; 17.1% on ≥3 BP-lowering drugs; 31% of them not at target).
claims.quote: 11,229 patients (17.1%) were on ≥3 BP- lowering medications [ 3]. Among this population, 69% achieved the BP target (systolic BP < 140 mmHg and diastolic BP < 90 mmHg), and 31% were not at target. Therefore, the estimated apparent treatment-RH among the Thai hypertensive population should be 5.3% of the treated population.

claims.claim: The true RH estimate for Thailand is around 3.4%, assuming the reported pseudo-RH prevalence of 33–37% among apparent treatment-RH applies to the Thai population.
claims.quote: There were reports estimating that the prevalence of pseudo-RH is between 33 and 37% among patients with apparent treatment-RH. Suppose the same is true in the Thai population. In that case, the estimated true RH in the Thai hypertensive population should be around 3.4%, lower than the estimation from a meta-analysis of observational studies in other populations

claims.claim: The conclusion restates true RH prevalence in Thai hypertensive populations as around 3.4% of the treated population.
claims.quote: True RH ’s estimated prevalence in Thai hypertensive populations should be around 3.4% of the treated population.

claims.claim: Separately, the consensus gives a general estimate of true RH of about 5% of the overall hypertensive population (from other populations).
claims.quote: excluding secondary hypertension, a reasonable estimate of the true RH should be about 5% of the overall hypertensive population [ 14].

cases.ambiguity: The phrase 'true resistant-hypertension prevalence' could refer either to the Thailand-specific estimate (~3.4% of the treated hypertensive population, assuming 33–37% pseudo-RH) or to the general estimate the consensus cites (~5% of the overall hypertensive population, assuming exclusion of white-coat effect, verified adherence, and no secondary hypertension). Both are reported in the answer.
